questions.q: The angle between lines joining the origin to the point of intersection of the line $\sqrt{3}$x+y=2$ and the curve $y^{2}-x^{2}=4$ is$
questions.solution:
On homogenising $y^{2}-x^{2}=4$ with the help of the line $\sqrt{3} x+y=2$, we get
$\begin{aligned}
& y^{2}-x^{2}=4 \frac{(\sqrt{3} x+y)^{2}}{4} \\
\Rightarrow & y^{2}-x^{2}=3 x^{2}+y^{2}+2 \sqrt{3} x y \\
\Rightarrow & 4 x^{2}+2 \sqrt{3} x y=0
\end{aligned}$
On comparing with $a x^{2}+2 h x y+b y^{2}=0$, we get
$\mathrm{a}=4, \mathrm{ h}=\sqrt{3} \text{$ and $} \mathrm{b}=0$
We know that,
$\tan \theta=2 \frac{\sqrt{\mathrm{h}^{2}-\mathrm{ab}}}{\mathrm{a}+\mathrm{b}}=\frac{2 \cdot \sqrt{3-0}}{4+0}\therefore \quad$ The angle between the lines is
$\theta=\tan ^{-1} \left(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right)$

Given that

Let $Z=x+i y$, then
$\begin{array}{l}
|x+i y-25|=5|x+i y-1| \\
\Rightarrow|(x-25)+i y|=5 \mid(x-1+i y \mid
\end{array}
Squaring both sides, we get
 $\begin{array}{l}
($\mathrm{x}-$25)^{2}+$\mathrm{y}^{2}=$25 $\left\{(\mathrm{x}-1$)^{2}+$\mathrm{y}^{2}\right\}$ \\
\Rightarrow $\mathrm{x}^{2}-$50 $\mathrm{x}+$625+$\mathrm{y}^{2}$ \\
\quad=25 $\mathrm{x}^{2}-$50 $\mathrm{x}+$25+25 $\mathrm{y}^{2}$ \\
\Rightarrow 24 $\mathrm{x}^{2}+$24 $\mathrm{y}^{2}-$600=0 \\
\Rightarrow $\mathrm{x}^{2}+\mathrm{y}^{2}-$25=0 \\
\Rightarrow|$\mathrm{x}+\mathrm{iy}$|^{2}=25 \Rightarrow|$\mathrm{Z}$|^{2}=5^{2} \\
\Rightarrow|$\mathrm{Z}$|=5
\end{array}

questions.q: The number of solutions of the equation $\sin \left(\mathrme^{\mathrm{x}}\right)=5^{\mathrm{x}}+5^{-\mathrm{x}}$, is
questions.solution:
We have, $\sin \left(e^{x}\right)=5^{x}+5^{-x}$...(i)
Let $5^{x}=t$, then eq. (i), reduces to

$\begin{array}{l}
$\sin $\left(e^{x}\right)$=t+$\frac{1}{t}$\\
\Rightarrow $\sin\left(e^{x}\right)=t+\frac{1}{t}-2$+2 \\
\Rightarrow $\sin \left(e^{x}\right)=\left(\sqrt{t}-\frac{1}{\sqrt{t}}\right)^{2}$+2 \\
\quad $\left\{5^{x}>0, \therefore \sqrt{5^{x}}=\sqrt{t} \text{ exists }\right\}$ \\
\Rightarrow $\sin\left(e^{x}\right)$ \geq 2
\end{array}$

questions.q: The pairs of straight lines $x^{2}-3 x y+2 y^{2}=0$ and $x^{2}-3 x y+2 y^{2}+x-2=0$ form $a$
questions.solution:
Given pair of lines are x^{2}-3 x y+2 y^{2}=0 and $x^{2}-3 x y+2 y^{2}+x-2=0
\therefore(x-2 y)(x-y)=0 and $(x-2 y+2)(x-y-1)=0\Rightarrow x-2 y=0, x-y=0$
and $x-2 y+2=0, x-y-1=0$
The lines $x-2 y=0, x-2 y+2=0$ and $x-y=0, x-y-1=0$ are paral lel.
Also, angle between $x-2 y=0$ and $x-y=0$ is not 90^{{}^{\circ}}\therefore$ It is a parallelogram.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The differential equation that represents all parabolas each of which has a latus rectum $4 a$ and whose axes are parallel to the $x$-axis is
questions.solution:
Equation of the family of such parabolas is $(\mathrm{y}-\mathrm{k})^{2}=4 \mathrm{a}(\mathrm{x}-\mathrm{h})$...(1)
where $\mathrm{h} \ \text{ and } \mathrm{k}$ are arbitrary constants Differentiating w.r.t. $x$, we get
$(\mathrm{y}-\mathrm{k}) \frac{\mathrm{dy}}{\mathrm{dx}}=2 \mathrm{a}$...(2)
Differentiating again
$(\mathrm{y}-\mathrm{k}) \frac{\mathrmd^{2} \mathrm{y}}{\mathrm{dx}^{2}}+\left(\frac{\mathrm{dy}}{\mathrm{dx}}\right)^{2}=0$...(3)
Putting value of $(y-k)$ from (2) in (3), we get
$2 \mathrm{a} \frac{\mathrmd^{2} \mathrm{y}}{\mathrm{dx}^{2}}+\left(\frac{\mathrm{dy}}{\mathrm{dx}}\right)^{3}=0$, which is required equation.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The angle between the tangents at those points on the curve $x=t^{2}+1$ and $y=t^{2}-t-6$ where it meets $\mathrm{x}$-axis is
questions.solution:
Equation of the given curve in parametric form,
$\mathrm{x}=\mathrm{t}^{2}+1$ and $\mathrm{y}=\mathrm{t}^{2}-\mathrm{t}-6$
Y-coordinate of the point, where the given curve meets $\mathrm{X}$-axis is 0 .
When $y=0$, then $t^{2}-t-6=0$
$\begin{array}{l}
\Rightarrow t^{2}-3 t+2 t-6=0 \\
\Rightarrow t(t-3)+2(t-3)=0 \\
\Rightarrow(t-3)(t+2)=0 \\
\Rightarrow t=3 \text { or }-2
\end{array}$
when $\mathrm{t}=3$, then $\mathrm{x}=10$
when $\mathrm{t}=-2$, then $\mathrm{x}=5$
Hence, the points where the curve meets the X-axis are $(10,0)$ and $(5,0)$.
Now, $\frac{\mathrm{dy}}{\mathrm{dx}}=\frac{\frac{\mathrm{dy}}{\mathrm{dt}}}{\frac{\mathrm{dx}}{\mathrm{dt}}}=\frac{2 \mathrm{t}-1}{2 \mathrm{t}}$
Slope of the tangent at point $(10,0)$
$\left.\left.\mathrm{m}_{1}=\frac{\mathrm{dy}}{\mathrm{dx}}\right]_{\mathrm{x}=10}=\frac{\mathrm{dy}}{\mathrm{dx}}\right]_{\mathrm{t}=3}=\frac{5}{6}$
Slope of the tangent at point $(5,0)$,
$\left.\left.\mathrm{m}_{2}=\frac{\mathrm{dy}}{\mathrm{dx}}\right]_{\mathrm{x}=5}=\frac{\mathrm{dy}}{\mathrm{dx}}\right]_{\mathrm{t}=-2}=\frac{-5}{-4}=\frac{5}{4}$
If $\theta$ be the angle beween two tangents, then
$\tan \theta=\left|\frac{\mathrm{m}_{2}-\mathrm{m}_{1}}{1+\mathrm{m}_{1} \mathrm{~m}_{2}}\right|=\left|\frac{\frac{5}{4}-\frac{5}{6}}{1+\frac{5}{6} \cdot \frac{5}{4}}\right|$
$\quad=\left|\frac{15-10}{\frac{12}{24+25}}\right|=\left|\frac{5}{\frac{12}{49}}\right|=\left|\frac{10}{49}\right|$
$\Rightarrow \tan \theta=\pm \frac{10}{49} \mid$
$\therefore \theta=\tan ^{-1}\left(\pm \frac{10}{49}\right)=\pm \tan ^{-1}\left(\frac{10}{49}\right)$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: To the lines $a x^{2}+2 h x y+b y^{2}=0$, the line $a^{2} x^{2}+2 h(a+b) x y+b^{2} y^{2}=0$ are
questions.solution:
The equation of the bisectors of the angle between the lines given by $a x^{2}+2 h x y+b y^{2}=0$ is $\frac{x^{2}-y^{2}}{a-b}=\frac{x y}{h}...($ i) And the equation of the bisectors of the angle between the lines given by $a^{2} x^{2}+2 h(a+b) x y+b^{2} y^{2}=0$ is $\begin{array}{l}\frac{x^{2}-y^{2}}{a^{2}-b^{2}}=\frac{x y}{h(a+b)}$\\
\Rightarrow $\frac{x^{2}-y^{2}}{a-b}=\frac{x}{h}...($ ii)
\end{array} From eqs. (i) and (ii), it is clear that both the pair of straight lines have the same bisector, hence, the given two pairs of straight lines are equally inclined.
